operative_clauses.original_operative_text: 1-101. There is established the President's Commission on Pension Policy. The Commission shall be composed of eleven members.

original_source.page_or_item: American Presidency Project web page (transcription; not an official edition); APP node 247767; common-crawl capture 2025-09-10T15:53:25Z; Sec. 1-101

operative_clauses.original_operative_text: 1-102. The members of the Commission shall be appointed by the President. The President shall designate a Chairman from among the members.

original_source.page_or_item: American Presidency Project web page (transcription; not an official edition); APP node 247767; common-crawl capture 2025-09-10T15:53:25Z; Sec. 1-102

operative_clauses.original_operative_text: 1-201. The Commission shall conduct a comprehensive review of retirement, survivor, and disability programs existing in the United States, including private, Federal, State and local programs.

original_source.page_or_item: American Presidency Project web page (transcription; not an official edition); APP node 247767; common-crawl capture 2025-09-10T15:53:25Z; Sec. 1-201

operative_clauses.original_operative_text: 1-202. The Commission shall develop national policies for retirement, survivor, and disability programs that can be used as a guide by public and private programs. Those policies must be designed to ensure that the Nation has effective and equitable retirement, survivor, and disability programs which take into account available resources and demographic changes that are expected into the middle of the next century.

original_source.page_or_item: American Presidency Project web page (transcription; not an official edition); APP node 247767; common-crawl capture 2025-09-10T15:53:25Z; Sec. 1-202

operative_clauses.original_operative_text: 1-203. The Commission shall submit to the President a series of reports. These reports shall include the Commission's findings and recommendations on short-term and long-term issues with respect to retirement, survivor, and disability programs, including, but not restricted to, the following:

original_source.page_or_item: American Presidency Project web page (transcription; not an official edition); APP node 247767; common-crawl capture 2025-09-10T15:53:25Z; Sec. 1-203 (lead-in)

operative_clauses.original_operative_text: (a) present overlaps and gaps among the private, State and local sectors in providing income to retired, surviving, and disabled persons;

original_source.page_or_item: American Presidency Project web page (transcription; not an official edition); APP node 247767; common-crawl capture 2025-09-10T15:53:25Z; Sec. 1-203(a)

operative_clauses.original_operative_text: (b) the financial ability of present private, Federal, State and local retirement, survivor, and disability systems to meet their future obligations;

original_source.page_or_item: American Presidency Project web page (transcription; not an official edition); APP node 247767; common-crawl capture 2025-09-10T15:53:25Z; Sec. 1-203(b)

operative_clauses.original_operative_text: (c) appropriate retirement ages, the relationship of the annuity levels to past earnings and contributions, and the role of current retirement, survivor, and disability programs in private capital formation and economic growth;

original_source.page_or_item: American Presidency Project web page (transcription; not an official edition); APP node 247767; common-crawl capture 2025-09-10T15:53:25Z; Sec. 1-203(c)

operative_clauses.original_operative_text: (d) the implications of the recommended national policies for the financing and benefit structures of the retirement, survivor, and disability programs in the public and private sectors; and

original_source.page_or_item: American Presidency Project web page (transcription; not an official edition); APP node 247767; common-crawl capture 2025-09-10T15:53:25Z; Sec. 1-203(d)

operative_clauses.original_operative_text: (e) specific reforms and organizational changes in the present systems that may be required to meet the goals of the national policies.

original_source.page_or_item: American Presidency Project web page (transcription; not an official edition); APP node 247767; common-crawl capture 2025-09-10T15:53:25Z; Sec. 1-203(e)

operative_clauses.original_operative_text: 1-204. The Commission shall submit its final report, including its recommendations and findings, to the President prior to its termination.

original_source.page_or_item: American Presidency Project web page (transcription; not an official edition); APP node 247767; common-crawl capture 2025-09-10T15:53:25Z; Sec. 1-204

operative_clauses.original_operative_text: 1-301. At the request of the Chairman each Executive agency that has an interest or responsibility in the areas of the Commission's functions shall designate an individual to act as liaison with the Commission and its staff.

original_source.page_or_item: American Presidency Project web page (transcription; not an official edition); APP node 247767; common-crawl capture 2025-09-10T15:53:25Z; Sec. 1-301

operative_clauses.original_operative_text: 1-302. In performing its functions, the Commission shall seek the advice of individuals and groups interested in policies applicable to retirement, survivor, and disability programs and systems. In seeking advice from interested individuals and groups, including public and private organizations, the Commission or any committee thereof, may, among other activities, hold hearings and sit and act at such times and places as the Commission or such authorized committee may find advisable.

original_source.page_or_item: American Presidency Project web page (transcription; not an official edition); APP node 247767; common-crawl capture 2025-09-10T15:53:25Z; Sec. 1-302

operative_clauses.original_operative_text: 1-303. The Commission may request any Executive agency to furnish such information as may be helpful for the fulfillment of the Commission's functions under this Order. Each such agency is authorized, to the extent permitted by law and within the limits of available funds, to furnish such information to the Commission.

original_source.page_or_item: American Presidency Project web page (transcription; not an official edition); APP node 247767; common-crawl capture 2025-09-10T15:53:25Z; Sec. 1-303

operative_clauses.original_operative_text: 1-304. The Commission is authorized to appoint and fix the compensation of a staff, including not more than one position at the GS-18 level, as may be necessary to enable it to carry out its functions. The Commission may obtain services in accordance with the provisions of Section 3109 of Title 5 of the United States Code, to the extent funds are available therefore.

original_source.page_or_item: American Presidency Project web page (transcription; not an official edition); APP node 247767; common-crawl capture 2025-09-10T15:53:25Z; Sec. 1-304

operative_clauses.original_operative_text: 1-305. Each member of the Commission who is not otherwise employed in the Government may receive, to the extent permitted by law, compensation for each day he or she is engaged upon the work of the Commission at a rate not to exceed the maximum daily rate now or hereafter prescribed by law for CS-18 of the General Schedule, and may also receive travel expenses, including per diem in lieu .of subsistence, as authorized by law (5 U.S.C. 5703) for persons in the government service employed intermittently.

original_source.page_or_item: American Presidency Project web page (transcription; not an official edition); APP node 247767; common-crawl capture 2025-09-10T15:53:25Z; Sec. 1-305

operative_clauses.original_operative_text: 1-306. The General Services Administration shall provide administrative services, facilities, and support to the Commission on a reimbursable basis.

original_source.page_or_item: American Presidency Project web page (transcription; not an official edition); APP node 247767; common-crawl capture 2025-09-10T15:53:25Z; Sec. 1-306

operative_clauses.original_operative_text: 1-307. All necessary expenses incurred in connection with the work of the Commission shall be paid from the appropriation for "Unanticipated Needs," in the Executive Office Appropriations Act, 1978, or from such other funds as may be available.

original_source.page_or_item: American Presidency Project web page (transcription; not an official edition); APP node 247767; common-crawl capture 2025-09-10T15:53:25Z; Sec. 1-307

operative_clauses.original_operative_text: 1-401. The functions of the President under the Federal Advisory Committee Act (5 U.S.C. App. 1), except that of reporting annually to the Congress, which are applicable to the Commission, shall be performed by the Administrator of General Services.

original_source.page_or_item: American Presidency Project web page (transcription; not an official edition); APP node 247767; common-crawl capture 2025-09-10T15:53:25Z; Sec. 1-401

operative_clauses.original_operative_text: 1-402. The Commission shall terminate one year after the effective date of this Order.

original_source.page_or_item: American Presidency Project web page (transcription; not an official edition); APP node 247767; common-crawl capture 2025-09-10T15:53:25Z; Sec. 1-402

operative_clauses.original_operative_text: 1-403. This Order shall be effective on the day of the first meeting .of the Commission members.

original_source.page_or_item: American Presidency Project web page (transcription; not an official edition); APP node 247767; common-crawl capture 2025-09-10T15:53:25Z; Sec. 1-403
